'''''Hydrangea paniculata''''', or '''panicled hydrangea''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Hydrangeaceae]] [[native plant|native]] to southern and eastern China, Korea, Japan and Russia ([[Sakhalin]]).<ref name=FoC/><ref>''Hydrangeas for American gardens'', by Dirr, Michael. Timber Press, 2004. {{ISBN|0881926418}}/{{ISBN|9780881926415}}</ref> It was first formally described by [[Philipp Franz von Siebold]] in 1829.<ref name=IPNI>{{IPNI|id=791653-1|accessdate=10 August 2009}}</ref>

==Description==

It is a [[deciduous]] shrub or small tree, {{convert|1|-|5|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|2.5|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} broad, growing in sparse forests or thickets in valleys or on mountain slopes.<ref name=FoC>{{cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200010123 |title=''Hydrangea paniculata'' |author=Wei Zhaofen |author2=Bruce Bartholomew |work=Flora of China |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden, St. Louis, MO & Harvard University Herbaria, Cambridge, MA |access-date=18 August 2012}}</ref>

The leaves are broadly oval, toothed and {{convert|7|-|15|cm|0|abbr=on}} long. In late summer it bears large conical panicles of creamy white fertile flowers, together with pinkish-white sterile florets. Florets may open pale green, grading to white with age, thus creating a pleasing "two-tone" effect.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1-4053-3296-5|pages=1136}}</ref>
[[File:Hydrangea paniculata 07-02-2026. (actm.).jpg|thumb|255px|  Dried petal of a Hydrangea paniculata on the bush in February.]]

* 'Praecox',<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pfeiffer|first=Sue A.|date=2009|title=Early Bloomer: Hydrangea paniculata 'Praecox'|url=http://arnoldia.arboretum.harvard.edu/pdf/articles/2009-67-1-early-bloomer-hydrangea-paniculata-praecox.pdf|journal=Arnoldia|volume=67|issue=1|page=44|doi=10.5962/p.251047 |access-date=2 October 2019}}</ref> a particularly early flowering cultivar

==Uses==

''Hydrangea paniculata'' is sometimes smoked as an intoxicant, despite the danger of illness and/or death due to the [[cyanide]]<ref>[http://www.erowid.org/herbs/hydrangea/hydrangea.shtml Erowid Hydrangea Vault]</ref>{{Unreliable source?|date=October 2020}} present as [[cyanogenic glycoside]]s.<ref>[http://www.aspca.org/pet-care/poison-control/plants/hills-of-snow.html ASPCA Animal Poison Control Center]</ref>

==Etymology==
''Hydrangea'' is derived from [[Greek language|Greek]], meaning 'water vessel', in reference to the shape of the capsules.<ref name="gledhill">Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  pp 206, 289</ref>

''Paniculata'' means 'with branched-racemose or cymose inflorescences', 'tufted', 'paniculate', or 'with panicles'. This name is about the flowers of this species.<ref name="gledhill" />
